name: David Brown
chief_complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and wheeze for 2 days
opening_statement: I can barely breathe... my inhaler isn't working anymore
emotional_baseline: Anxious and struggling to speak in full sentences

symptoms.name: Dyspnoea
symptoms.onset: Progressive worsening over 48 hours, now severe at rest
symptoms.character: Sensation of air hunger, unable to lie flat
symptoms.associations: Audible wheeze, chest tightness, dry cough
symptoms.time_course: Continuous, worse at night and early morning

citations.quote: Severe exacerbation characterized by breathlessness at rest, speaks in words only, respiratory rate >25/min
Widespread wheeze indicates severe airway obstruction requiring urgent treatment

symptoms.name: Chest tightness
symptoms.associations: Worse with inspiration, relief only partial with salbutamol
symptoms.time_course: Persistent, no relief in last 12 hours

citations.quote: Chest tightness commonly accompanies acute asthma and reflects bronchospasm

symptoms.name: Cough
symptoms.associations: Triggered by talking or cold air

citations.quote: Cough may be the predominant symptom in some asthma exacerbations

past_medical_history.severity: Moderate persistent, previous ICU admission 3 years ago
past_medical_history.current_status: Usually well controlled, 2-3 exacerbations per year requiring oral steroids

medications.name: Budesonide/formoterol (Symbicort) 200/6
medications.adherence: Good until 3 days ago when ran out

medications.name: Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler
medications.frequency: PRN, now using every 30 minutes with minimal relief
medications.adherence: Excessive current use - nearly empty canister in 2 days

allergies: Penicillin (reported rash as child, never re-challenged), grass pollen, house dust mites
family_history: Mother has asthma (well controlled), father has hypertension, sister has eczema and allergic rhinitis, no family history of COPD or lung cancer

social_history.alcohol: Social drinker, 4-6 standard drinks per week
social_history.exercise: Usually walks 30 minutes 3-4 times weekly, unable currently
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and 2 children (ages 8 and 11) in suburban house
social_history.recent_exposures: School setting, increased spring pollen count this week, classroom painting 4 days ago
social_history.functional_status: Independent in ADLs when well, currently requires assistance for basic tasks

examination_findings.general: Distressed male, sitting upright and forward, speaking in 3-4 word sentences, appears exhausted

respiratory.inspection: Use of accessory muscles, intercostal recession, unable to complete sentences
respiratory.palpation: Trachea central, reduced chest expansion bilaterally
respiratory.auscultation: Bilateral widespread expiratory wheeze, reduced air entry throughout, prolonged expiratory phase

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, normal heart sounds, no murmurs, JVP not elevated
examination_findings.other: No cyanosis, no peripheral oedema, no clubbing

arterial_blood_gas.interpretation: Type 1 respiratory failure, normocapnia concerning for impending respiratory failure

expected_results.chest_xray: Hyperinflation, no focal consolidation, no pneumothorax

actions: High-flow oxygen via Hudson mask targeting SpO2 93-95%
Salbutamol 12 puffs via spacer immediately, repeat every 20 minutes
Ipratropium bromide 8 puffs via spacer
Prednisolone 50mg PO or hydrocortisone 100mg IV if unable to swallow
Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiac monitoring
Establish IV access
If no improvement after 1 hour: Consider continuous nebulised salbutamol
If deteriorating: Alert ICU, prepare for non-invasive ventilation or intubation
Rising PaCO2 or altered mental state = life-threatening asthma requiring ICU
Hospital admission (acute severe asthma, high-risk patient)
Continue regular salbutamol (can transition to 4-hourly nebulisers once improving)
Continue ipratropium bromide 6-hourly for 24-48 hours
Oral prednisolone 50mg daily for 5-7 days
MBS item 23 (comprehensive hospital consultation)
Consider IV magnesium sulfate 2g over 20 minutes if poor response
Restart ICS/LABA preventer (ensure PBS authority if needed)
Provide written asthma action plan
GP follow-up within 2 days of discharge
Respiratory physician review within 4 weeks
Address trigger avoidance (workplace exposure)
Assess inhaler technique
Smoking cessation counselling (if applicable - N/A here)
MBS item 721 (asthma cycle of care incentive payment for GP)

critical_errors.error: Failure to administer high-flow oxygen immediately
critical_errors.rationale: SpO2 89% represents severe hypoxaemia requiring urgent correction to prevent end-organ damage

critical_errors.error: Failure to administer systemic corticosteroids within first hour
critical_errors.rationale: Corticosteroids are essential in acute severe asthma; delay worsens outcomes and prolongs hospital stay

critical_errors.error: Discharge home without hospital admission despite severe markers (PEFR 33%, SpO2 89%, normocapnia)
critical_errors.rationale: Life-threatening asthma with high risk of respiratory arrest; requires hospital monitoring
Respiratory depressants can precipitate respiratory failure in severe asthma

critical_errors.error: Failure to arrange escalation plan or ICU alert for deteriorating patient
critical_errors.rationale: Normocapnia in severe asthma is warning sign of impending respiratory failure requiring urgent senior review

critical_errors.error: Not addressing medication non-adherence (ran out of preventer)
critical_errors.rationale: Likely precipitant of exacerbation; must be addressed to prevent recurrence

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (Respiratory Medicine), Staff Specialist, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital
fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent representation of acute severe asthma with appropriate risk stratification. The normocapnia on ABG is a critical clinical teaching point - candidates must recognise this as a warning sign rather than reassurance. Workplace trigger (classroom painting) is realistic and tests occupational history-taking. Difficulty calibration is appropriate for medium level.
fracp_reviews.suggested_improvements: None - this scenario meets AMC Clinical Examination standards for respiratory medicine assessment.

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (General & Respiratory Medicine), Director of Emergency Medicine, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne
fracp_reviews.comments: Clinically accurate scenario that tests critical decision-making in life-threatening asthma. The 4 critical errors appropriately reflect auto-fail management gaps that would lead to adverse outcomes. The inclusion of previous ICU admission elevates risk and tests risk stratification skills. MBS items correctly cited (item 23, item 721).
fracp_reviews.suggested_improvements: Consider adding peak flow monitoring response to treatment as a learning point, but not essential for medium difficulty scenario.

learning_objectives.objective: Recognise features of acute severe and life-threatening asthma
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Differentiate severity markers: PEFR 33-50% (severe), SpO2 <92% (severe), speaking in words only (life-threatening). Normal PaCO2 in severe asthma indicates impending respiratory failure (inability to maintain hyperventilation).

learning_objectives.objective: Initiate time-critical management of acute severe asthma
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Oxygen + bronchodilators + corticosteroids within first hour. Escalate to continuous nebulisers/IV magnesium/ICU if no response to initial therapy.

learning_objectives.objective: Identify high-risk asthma patients requiring admission
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Previous ICU admission, poor perception of severity, rapid deterioration, PEFR <50%, SpO2 <92% all mandate hospital admission even if improves with initial treatment.

learning_objectives.objective: Recognise asthma triggers and preventable precipitants
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Allergen exposure (pollen season), medication non-adherence (ran out of preventer), occupational exposures (classroom painting) are modifiable risk factors requiring systematic assessment.
Use of ICS/LABA preventer, written asthma action plans, cycle of care arrangements (MBS item 721), PBS restrictions for biologics if severe uncontrolled asthma.

learning_objectives.objective: Interpret arterial blood gases in acute asthma
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Initial hyperventilation causes respiratory alkalosis. Normocapnia or hypercapnia in severe asthma = exhaustion and impending respiratory failure requiring urgent escalation.

learning_objectives.objective: Assess inhaler technique and adherence barriers
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Medication non-adherence is leading cause of asthma exacerbations. Running out of preventer suggests systems failure (prescription access, cost, understanding) requiring targeted intervention.

learning_objectives.objective: Plan safe discharge and follow-up for acute asthma
learning_objectives.clinical_reasoning: Ensure 5-7 days oral steroids, restart preventer, written action plan, GP review <2 days, specialist review <4 weeks. Address workplace trigger before return to work.
